messages:
maria: Heads up — canary pool in us-west-2 started failing after we pushed the toolkit12 image this morning. Nodes hang in provisioning and several containers exit with JIT/PTX errors.

aj: yep, saw the flurry. grabbing logs now. this looks like a runtime/driver mismatch — cuda symbols missing at load time.

aj: paste of the container stderr:```
/opt/conda/lib/python3.10/site-packages/torch/csrc/cuda/Module.cpp:54: error: jitlink: failed to open ptx cache: Permission denied
E tensorflow/stream_executor/cuda/cuda_driver.cc:xx] failed to allocate 64MB (cuInit returned error)
ldd /workspace/bin/worker | grep libcuda -> libcuda.so.1 => /usr/local/nvidia/lib64/libcuda.so.1 (0x00007f...)
undefined symbol: cuDevicePrimaryCtxRetain_v2
```

ops-bot: deployment-checker: canary-deploy/rtx-pool triggered rollback due to >20% node provisioning errors :rotating_light: (auto-rollback engaged)

maria: rollback is fine as short-term, but we need root cause. this is hitting CI and some production canaries.

vivek: initial hypothesis: containers were built with gcc13 and CUDA 12 toolchain; host nodes still on driver/runtime combo that exposes older symbols. JIT (ptx) path compiles kernels at load — if libcuda/driver ABI differs it errors out.

kevin: confirmed on one repro node: kernel headers missing for the host's running kernel. that causes the nvidia module not to provide certain ioctl/symbols and then the driver shim produces odd undefined symbols.

aj: repro steps i used: spin baremetal canary -> pull toolkit12 image -> run sample cuda program -> immediate fatal with messages above. quick ldd and nm show symbols by name mismatched.

maria: is this limited to us-west-2?

aj: so far only observed in us-west-2 and ap-southeast canaries. other regions still fine (likely because their host drivers were bumped during last maintenance).

sre-oncall: we have limited spare nodes in ap-southeast so we should avoid big rebuilds there. canary rollback bought time but cost of rebuilding all images and pushing is non-trivial.

kevin: short mitigation that worked on one node: restart nvidia-modprobe after ensuring kernel-headers present, then restart kubelet so node re-registers with proper driver capabilities. that made the sample program progress past JIT stage. not a universal fix.

aj: another mitigation: set env var NV_JIT_CACHE_DISABLE=1 for the worker to bypass the PTX cache path (temporary), it let the job start but performance regressed and it caused more memory pressure.

maria: note: setting NV_JIT_CACHE_DISABLE is just a band-aid. we need a triage plan.

v ivek: proposed plan: 1) inventory nodes to find host driver versions and kernel header presence, 2) mark suspect nodes as drain-once for a maintenance pass, 3) bump driver on a small canary subset to the toolkit12-compatible minimum and run chaos checks, 4) schedule full rollout only after green.

maria: agree. add step 0: stop new toolkit12 image pushes and tag current images as blocked in registry (prevent accidental redeploys).

deploy-bot: image-promotion: tag redwood/toolkit:12-edge -> BLOCKED_BY_INCIDENT #incident-1777777000

kevin: cost note — driver/provisioning windows will force node reboots and may temporarily reduce capacity. finance: expect an extra ~8-12% on hosting for the week if we expedite kernels/drivers on many hosts.

maria: @sre-oncall can you scope outage risk and earliest timeline for a minimal driver bump in us-west-2?

sre-oncall: i can run a small driver bump tomorrow morning in the 02:00-06:00 UTC window, limited to 10 nodes. need approval to escalate to infra maintenance.

aj: i'll prep a small canary image that disables JIT cache and uses a pre-bundled nvrtc/libdevice so it doesn't rely on host PTX compile path. will test in isolated pool.

v ivek: also add a post-deploy probe that runs a quick PTX/JIT smoke test and NCCL allreduce to catch subtle runtime regressions.

maria: good. action items:
- aj: build and test JIT-disabled experiment image in isolated pool (ETA 3h)
- sre-oncall: schedule 10-node driver bump canary (ETA tomorrow window)
- kevin: inventory script to list driver versions + kernel-headers (ETA 2h)
- vivek: prepare rollback checklist + perf delta expectations if we keep NV_JIT_CACHE_DISABLE (ETA 4h)

aj: starting on build now. will post repro details.

kevin: i pushed an inventory script to infra-runbooks; running now against us-west-2. found ~23 nodes with missing headers and driver packages out of date.

maria: ok; thanks. keep thread updated. if we see any region spike, we'll open a pager.

ops-bot: incident-1777777000 created (severity: high) — follow runbook: toolkit-upgrade-fallback

aj: quick repro logs and a workaround snippet i used on a node:```bash
sudo apt-get install linux-headers-$(uname -r)
sudo systemctl restart nvidia-modprobe
sudo systemctl restart kubelet
# then cordon & uncordon after kubelet re-register
```

maria: concise note to docs team: add a permanent checklist for toolkit upgrades: host-driver matrix, kernel headers verification, and canary gating hooks.

kevin: adding that to infra-runbook now.

sre-oncall: will post schedule once approved.

maria: thanks all. keep replies short here — we want focused actions.

aj: will post a short summary + links to repro artifacts in 1 hour.

kevin: inventory results saved -> s3://infra-ops/toolkit12/inventory/us-west-2-1777777000.json

maria: closing for now, we'll reopen if rollback fails or more regions pop. :thumbsup:
